note: NYC: 4.5% city + 0.375% MCTD transit surcharge on top of 4% state. Destination-based. Uniform across NYC ZIPs.
CA is mixed-sourcing: state/county/city origin-based, district taxes destination-based. LA County district add-ons push downtown LA to ~9.75%; other LA-county ZIPs differ.
Cook County + Chicago + RTA transit district stack to 10.25%, among the highest big-city rates. IL intrastate origin-based; remote sellers destination-based (2026 rules tightened).
TX caps local add-ons at 2.0% (city 1% + Houston MTA transit 1%). TX is origin-based for intrastate sales. 8.25% is the statewide max.
FL 6% state + Miami-Dade 1% discretionary surtax. FL surtax applies to first $5,000 of a single tangible item on some categories. Destination-based.
WA 6.5% state + King County/Seattle + Sound Transit RTA district = ~10.25-10.35%. Destination-based. Some downtown blocks carry extra stadium/transit add-ons.
NOMAD state. No sales or use tax for buyers. DE instead levies a seller-side gross receipts tax. Every DE ZIP = 0%.
NOMAD state. No state or local sales tax anywhere in OR. Every OR ZIP = 0%.
FL 6% + Palm Beach County 0.5% surtax. Lower than Miami-Dade. FL county surtaxes vary widely (0%-1.5%), so FL ZIP rates differ by county.

CO has the lowest state rate (2.9%) but heavy local stacking: Denver city + RTD transit + cultural facilities district. CO is a notorious home-rule/multi-jurisdiction state; ZIP rates are especially unreliable here.
GA 4% + Fulton County LOST/SPLOST + Atlanta MARTA transit + city add-ons = ~8.9%. GA ZIPs frequently span multiple counties (classic multi-jurisdiction problem).
MA has NO local sales taxes; the 6.25% state rate is uniform statewide. One of the few states where ZIP = state rate everywhere. (Meals tax is separate.)

AZ 5.6% state + Maricopa County 0.7% + Phoenix city TPT. Phoenix raised its city rate ~0.5% (8.6% -> 9.1%) effective Oct 2025, so 9.1% is the current 2026 combined rate. AZ uses Transaction Privilege Tax (seller-side), origin/special sourcing.
OK 4.5% state + Oklahoma County + OKC city. OK allows local option up to ~6.5%; OKC combined ~8.625%. OK ZIPs cross county lines often. Verify against OK Tax Commission quarterly rate charts.

LA has the highest average combined US rate (~10.1%). Orleans Parish local ~5% on top of 5% state = ~10%. LA local sales tax is administered at the parish level, making rooftop accuracy especially important.
NM uses a Gross Receipts Tax (GRT), now destination-based (since Jul 1, 2021). State portion 4.875% + Santa Fe city/county = ~8.19%. NM rates use 4-decimal precision and change frequently.
NV 6.85% state (includes mandatory statewide LSST/BCCRT components) + Clark County add-ons = 8.375%. Clark County (Las Vegas) is NV's highest. Destination-based.

NOMAD state: no AK state sales tax. Anchorage levies NO local sales tax = 0%. BUT 100+ other AK localities DO (up to ~7.5%, e.g., Juneau, Wasilla, Kodiak), often collected via the ARSSTC remote-seller commission. AK ZIP rate is purely local.
RI has NO local sales tax; 7% state rate is uniform statewide (like MA). Included as a second 'state-rate-equals-ZIP-rate' example. Destination-based.
